clue.text: Drainage channel not charming initially to Lake Poet

indicators.note: to means one piece is attached to the other, giving the order of the charade

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out of the channel word

parts.note: a ditch is a drainage channel

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word charming

explanation.surface: A poet of the Lake District, describing a dull drainage ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake Poet' suggests Wordsworth or Coleridge, but Lake is MERE and the poet is George Meredith. 'not ... initially' removes C, the first letter of 'charming', from DITCH to leave DITH.
explanation.definitionFit: George Meredith was a Victorian novelist and poet, so the bare word poet defines him by example.

clue.text: Parent's restaurant's opening to feed Al cheese

parts.note: Ma is a parent; with the 's she gives MA and S

indicators.note: to feed means the restaurant letter goes inside the gangster's surname

parts.note: Al stands for Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, giving his surname

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of restaurant

explanation.surface: A parent's restaurant opens up to feed someone called Al some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Al' is not a friend at dinner but the Chicago gangster; 'to feed' puts the restaurant's opening letter inside his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascarpone is a soft, creamy Italian cheese, used in tiramisu, so it is an example of a cheese.

clue.text: Steak not finished? That's odd

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter of the cut of meat is dropped

parts.note: rump steak is a cut of beef, so steak can give rump

explanation.surface: A diner complains that a steak left uneaten is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' cuts the last letter, P, from RUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is an informal British word for strange or peculiar, as in a rum business.

clue.text: Having broken end, roof is ruined

indicators.note: having broken signals that the letters of the two words are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A house whose roof has collapsed at one end is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having broken' turns the letters of END and ROOF into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To be done for is an idiom meaning doomed or finished, effectively ruined.

clue.text: Specially arranges table, one beautifully dressed

parts.note: to tailor something is to adapt or arrange it for a special purpose
in bridge the dummy is the hand laid face up on the table

explanation.surface: Someone carefully lays a table, and one guest is elegantly dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the dummy is the declarer's partner's hand, spread face up on the table, so 'table' leads there.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's dummy is a model torso on which clothes are fitted, so it is always well dressed.

clue.text: Time to take utensil out? Exactly

indicators.note: to take means the time letter is taken into the utensil word
out means the utensil word sits outside, around the time letter

parts.note: a spoon is a kitchen utensil

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it is time to take out the cutlery; quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' and 'out' together put T inside SPOON, the utensil around it; the surface's 'take utensil out' suggests emptying a drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is a British idiom for exactly right or precisely accurate.

clue.text: Piano that's plain black and white

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is
bald means plain or unadorned, as in a bald statement

explanation.surface: A piano that is simply black and white, keys and case alike.
explanation.walkthrough: IE stands for 'id est', that is.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald horse has patches of black and white, so the colours describe it.

clue.text: Follow arsonist: there's no one ahead of him

definitions.text: there's no one ahead of him

parts.note: to trail someone is to follow them
a blazer is jokingly someone who sets blazes, an arsonist

explanation.surface: Detectives shadow a firestarter who is out in front of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: BLAZER is a whimsical coinage, one who makes blazes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer who blazes a trail goes first, so nobody is ahead of such a leader.

clue.text: Dead central point ——- mass in it

indicators.note: in it means the mass letter is put inside the central point word

parts.note: the nub is the central point of a matter
m is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A dead centre point with a mass placed at it, like a physics diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A numb limb has lost all feeling, so it is dead in the everyday sense of insensible.

clue.text: Holding a book, half-clear at first about what words mean

indicators.note: holding means the half and clear pieces wrap around the book pieces

parts.note: semi- is a prefix meaning half
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

indicators.note: at first picks the first letter of clear

explanation.surface: Someone holds a book, half-cleared at first, puzzling over what the words mean.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'half-clear' must be ignored: 'half' and 'clear at first' are separate pieces, and 'Holding' wraps them round A and the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantic means relating to meaning in language, so it describes what concerns the sense of words.

clue.text: Deprive of air? Don't panic

definitions.meaning: to deprive of moving air, as wind dropping leaves a sailing ship stuck
the command 'stay composed', split as two words

explanation.surface: Someone about to be starved of air is told not to panic.
explanation.walkthrough: Air here is wind, not breath: a ship in a calm has no wind to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A becalmed ship has no wind, and the phrase split into two words is an order to stay composed.

clue.text: Getting through night, it's dawn breaking

indicators.note: breaking signals the letters are broken up and rearranged, while also suggesting daybreak

explanation.surface: Someone surviving the night is relieved that dawn is breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' looks like part of 'dawn breaking' but rearranges NIGHT, ITS and DAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand is to endure, so withstanding means getting through a hardship.

clue.text: Avoiding computers entirely on holiday

parts.note: to keep away from something is to avoid it
IT is information technology, the world of computers
all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker steers clear of computers altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting away from it all is the idiom for escaping daily routine, which is what being on holiday is.

clue.text: Credit Papa —- fancy securing English rose

indicators.note: securing means the jumbled letters hold the English letter inside them
fancy as an adjective means elaborate, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Credit is given to a father whose fancy English rose wins praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges the first two words; 'securing' puts E inside that. 'English rose' looks like a flower or a woman, but rose is the verb, went up in value.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset that appreciated rose in value, so the past tense verb matches.

clue.text: Concerned with sons, outwardly stupid, showing sporting talent

indicators.note: outwardly means the stupid word sits on the outside, wrapped round the other pieces

parts.note: dense means stupid or slow-witted
re means concerning or about
s abbreviates son; the plural is taken here as three of them

explanation.surface: Sons who seem dim on the outside nonetheless show talent at sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' means wearing, not athletic: the talent is for showing off clothes. 'showing' is a link. 'sons' gives three Ss, an unspecified plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress sense is a flair for choosing what to wear, a talent for sporting clothes well.

clue.text: One playing quietly in support

indicators.note: in means the quiet letter goes inside the support word

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge
p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A musician plays softly in a supporting role.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is a musician who plays the bagpipes, so one playing describes him.

clue.text: Planner in hut said rule has been broken

indicators.note: said means the hut word is heard as spoken, with its spelling changed

parts.note: a shed is a hut

indicators.note: has been broken signals the letters of rule are rearranged

explanation.surface: Inside a garden shed, someone declares that a regulation has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: SCHED- is said like SHED in the British way of saying the word; 'has been broken' turns RULE into ULER.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheduler draws up timetables, so is a planner of events.

clue.text: Perforce is short of grape juice

parts.note: someone who is short of something needs it
must is unfermented grape juice

explanation.surface: Of necessity, there is not enough grape juice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs must' is from the proverb 'needs must when the devil drives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce means by necessity, and the proverbial phrase means one must do what necessity dictates.

clue.text: Carry us over dirty patch

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word us is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a stain is a dirty mark or patch

explanation.surface: An instruction to take us across a muddy stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns US into SU above STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a weight is to bear or carry it.

clue.text: Manages to catch one very brief sleep?

definitions.text: Manages to catch one very brief sleep?

indicators.note: to catch means the managing word holds the sleep letter inside

parts.note: does means manages, as in 'that does it'
a single Z, from the cartoon ZZZ of snoring, is a very short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone contrives to grab a quick nap.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray 0. The whole clue defines dozing as grabbing a little sleep, and builds it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozes means sleeps lightly for short spells, which is managing to catch brief sleep.

clue.text: Make income last for poor old lady

parts.note: do means make, as in do a meal
a wage is income from work

indicators.note: last for picks the final letter of poor

explanation.surface: Advice to stretch one's income to support a poor elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like a verb, make income last, but it takes the final letter R of 'poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, so an old lady, informally.

clue.text: Lengthy screed is written so precisely

definitions.meaning: a long piece of writing is set down using a great quantity of vocabulary
explicitly or exactly, as in saying something plainly

explanation.surface: A long tirade is written in exactly this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: a long screed uses a large number of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means explicitly or precisely, and literally describes a long text full of words.

clue.text: Being married, like hot brew

parts.note: as means like
h is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Being married is said to be like a hot brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is the brewer's mixture of malt and hot water, so is a brew, or to mash tea is to brew it.

clue.text: Stone set in a sea, like a star

indicators.note: set in means the stone abbreviation is placed inside the sea

parts.note: the Aral Sea lies in Central Asia
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A gem set in a sea, glittering like a star.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone (ST) is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral means of or relating to the stars, so it means star-like.

clue.text: Play a card: jack of hearts nice to begin with

parts.note: a king is a court card in the pack
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

indicators.note: to begin with picks the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A card player lays down a card, then the jack of hearts, a good start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb about cards but names a Shakespeare history play.
explanation.definitionFit: King John is one of Shakespeare's history plays, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: Gold mine finally a source of metal

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of mine

explanation.surface: A gold mine is, in the end, a source of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is rock from which metal is extracted, so it is a source of metal.

clue.text: Telling off, not initially thrashing

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the scolding word is dropped

parts.note: chiding is scolding or telling off

explanation.surface: A scolding, short of an actual beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops C from CHIDING.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a beating, as in giving someone a good hiding.

clue.text: In terrible rage, give distress

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Flying into a terrible rage causes others distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the letters of RAGE and GIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve someone is to distress or wrong them.
